question:
A 36-year-old otherwise healthy man comes to the emergency department with a 3-day history of
progressive redness, pain, and swelling around his left elbow. Four days ago, he was working in his
attic, crawling on his elbows and knees, and afterward noticed scratches on these areas. He has no
history of joint swelling, and no other joints are involved. He denies fevers, chills, or other systemic
symptoms and feels well overall. On examination, his temperature is 38.1°C, heart rate is 74 beats per
minute, and blood pressure is 127/82 mm Hg. There is significant erythema and swelling over the
posterior elbow with a boggy fluid collection. The elbow can fully extend, but flexion is painful and
limited. Aspiration of the olecranon bursa yields 8 mL of mildly cloudy yellow fluid with a leukocyte
count of 6000 per mm³, no crystals, and a negative Gram stain. What is the most appropriate
management for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Ceftriaxone and azithromycin (B) Naproxen (C) Oral
clindamycin (D) Oral doxycycline (E) Surgical debridement (F) Dicloxacillin (G) Warm compresses (H)
Intravenous vancomycin (I) Observation without treatment (J) Aspiration and corticosteroid injection
 A. Oral clindamycin
B. Surgical debridement
C. Oral doxycycline
D. Intravenous vancomycin
E. Observation without treatment
F. Ceftriaxone and azithromycin
G. Aspiration and corticosteroid injection
H. Naproxen
I. Dicloxacillin
J. Warm compresses
